questions.text: What is the register map of the test shell (offset, width, reset value and access of every register)?
questions.default: Offsets 0x00 to 0x28 as in registers.map, 32-bit each.
questions.reason: The request names shell registers (tick, take, reply length and words, status) but gives no offsets.
questions.answer:
IN: offset 0x00, WO, reset 0: [7:0] packet byte, [8] end flag
STAT: offset 0x09, RO, reset 0: [0] telemetry on, [1] busy
RIDX: offset 0x03, RW, reset 0: [6:0] word number
RWORD: offset 0x04, RO, reset 0: bytes 4i..4i+3 of the reply, first byte on top, zero past the end
RLEN: offset 0x02, RO, reset 0: length in bytes of the latest reply, 0 if none
TICK: offset 0x01, WO, reset 0: [7:0] n ticks
TIDX: offset 0x06, RW, reset 0: [6:0] word number
TWORD: offset 0x07, RO, reset 0: same for the telemetry frame
TAKE: offset 0x08, WO, reset 0: any write takes the held telemetry frame
TLEN: offset 0x05, RO, reset 0: length of the held telemetry frame, 0 if none
shell: test shell, PROTOCOL.md 1.1
unmapped: no register at an offset: reads 0, writes ignored (read-only registers behave the same on write)
questions.evidence: IN: offset 0x00, WO, reset 0: [7:0] packet byte, [8] end flag

questions.text: Do unknown-type, wrong-length and register-error replies carry a payload?
questions.reason: Request defines payload only for read and status replies.

questions.text: Is a status reply 16 or 17 bytes of payload?
questions.reason: The text says sixteen bytes and one more, which sums to 17.
questions.answer: 17 bytes: seven 16-bit counters (14 bytes), the 16-bit telemetry frame count (2 bytes), and the TLM_ON byte (1 byte).
questions.evidence: STATUS: seven 16-bit counters, telemetry frame count (16 bit), TLM_ON byte, all before this command is counted.

questions.text: Does the held frame get counted in the frame count when taken or when held?
questions.reason: Request says counts rise only when a frame is held.
questions.answer: When held. The frame count changes only when a frame is held, so the default is correct.
questions.evidence: Frame sequence and frame count change only when a frame is held and only reset clears them.
